reasoning_records.title: TSMC Valuation Based on P/E Range, Not Fixed Multiple
claims: TSMC's intrinsic value hasn't changed significantly over time
Market sentiment drives P/E multiple fluctuations, not fundamentals
observations: TSMC's stock price can vary widely even if earnings remain stable
Current P/E for TSMC is estimated between 20x and 30x due to market optimism
reasoning_steps: P/E ratio = Stock Price / EPS
EPS provides a consistent measure of profitability
Market assigns higher P/E during bullish sentiment (e.g., post-QE)
Thus, same EPS can justify different prices based on sentiment
assumptions: TSMC continues to execute on its long-term technology roadmap
Global semiconductor demand remains structurally strong
conditions: If market sentiment shifts from 'strong buy' to neutral, P/E could revert to 15x–20x range
risks: Buying at peak P/E (e.g., 30x) risks multi-year stagnation even if fundamentals hold
exceptions: Long-term holders may tolerate stagnation; risk mainly affects new buyers
decisions_or_preferences: Caution against new entries at current high valuations
actions_or_avoided_actions: Avoid chasing TSMC at market highs
Do not assume high P/E justifies infinite upside

reasoning_records.title: Central Bank Intervenes to Weaken TWD Despite Natural Strengthening
claims: TWD strengthens due to global capital inflows seeking yield
Central bank actively sells USD daily in afternoon to weaken TWD
observations: TWD fell from 30 to 29.2 despite strong fundamentals
Daily long lower shadows on TWD chart indicate intervention
reasoning_steps: Global QE → excess liquidity → capital seeks higher-yielding markets
Taiwan offers high dividend yields → attracts inflows → increases TWD demand
Strong TWD hurts exporters → central bank intervenes to weaken currency
Intervention creates 'willow tree' chart pattern with long lower wicks
assumptions: Export competitiveness is a primary policy goal
Capital inflows will continue under global low-rate environment
risks: U.S. may designate Taiwan as currency manipulator
U.S. could impose penalties or force negotiations
conditions: If U.S. political pressure increases, intervention may stop
decisions_or_preferences: Expect continued intervention unless external pressure mounts

reasoning_records.title: High Dividend Yield Attracts Capital in Low-Interest Environment
claims: High-dividend stocks become relative value plays when rates fall
Capital inflows can push up prices even if fundamentals don't change
observations: 5% dividend yield is attractive when bank rates are near zero
Price appreciation can compress yield but rewards early investors
reasoning_steps: Investor requires 5% return
Bank deposits offer <1%
Stock with 5% yield becomes attractive
Demand increases → price rises → yield compresses (e.g., from 5% to 2.5%)
But original investor locks in high yield
conditions: If rates rise, dividend appeal diminishes

reasoning_records.title: Prefer Low-Cost Index ETFs Over Actively Managed or Strategy-Based ETFs
claims: ETF fees are the most important selection criterion
Strategy-based ETFs (e.g., 00850) embed active management despite appearing passive
observations: Many investors choose ETFs to avoid stock-picking risk
Yet they select actively managed ETFs that contradict this rationale
reasoning_steps: Index ETFs (e.g., 0050, 006208) passively track market
Strategy ETFs (e.g., 00850, 0056) involve human stock selection
If you believe individuals can't beat the market, why choose an ETF with active selection?
Therefore, prioritize low-cost index ETFs
assumptions: Active management adds cost without reliable outperformance
decisions_or_preferences: Tolerate holding both index and strategy ETFs for experimentation
actions_or_avoided_actions: Avoid justifying strategy ETFs solely by past performance

reasoning_records.title: OTA Platforms More Resilient Than Hotel Operators During Travel Downturn
claims: Asset-light business models (e.g., Booking.com) outperform asset-heavy ones (e.g., hotels) in crises
Stock prices reflect real business risk over time
observations: OTA platforms like BKNG show meaningful recovery
reasoning_steps: Hotels have high fixed costs (real estate, staff)
OTAs are software platforms with lower fixed costs
During downturn, high fixed costs → cash burn → bankruptcy risk
Thus, market prices hotels lower due to structural risk
assumptions: Travel recovery will be slow and uncertain
Investors price in long-term survival risk
risks: Overestimating recovery speed of physical travel assets
exceptions: Taiwan hotels less affected due to domestic tourism rebound
decisions_or_preferences: Prefer OTAs over direct hotel investments in uncertain recovery
